title: Grateful Dead Live at Veterans' Memorial Coliseum on 1982-09-23
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Samplitude Professional v11.03 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Clear soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1982 show with a smoking Wheel > Wharf Rat > Other One sequence and a killer Althea.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean soundboard mix that lets the band’s 1982 fire shine through, especially on the Wheel–Wharf Rat–Other One stretch and an electric Althea. Reviewers rave about Jerry’s soaring guitar work, Brent’s B‑3 presence and strong overall playing, while noting the bass sits a bit low in the mix but is still audible.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers (9/11) give 4‑5 stars and praise both performance and recording; only one clear negative outlier. Show quality is rated very high, recording quality good to excellent.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp soundboard with clear instrument separation; Phil’s bass a bit low in the mix but balanced by Charlie Miller’s mastering. A few listeners note slight tape‑speed quirks that make some songs feel fast, but overall the audio is clean and listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set flows seamlessly; the Wheel‑Wharf Rat‑Other One sequence and Althea are highlighted as high points, with a lively encore that kept even the concession staff dancing.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Playing is on fire – great tone on Little Red Rooster, electric solo at the end of Althea and overall strong vocals.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass sits low in the mix (typical for this era) but Miller’s mastering brings it forward enough; no major performance complaints.
band_member_comments.Bob: Slide guitar was criticized early in the show, though some reviewers feel his work on Althea adds to its power.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (on B‑3) is prominently featured and praised for solid organ work throughout the set.
